historical_references.reference: Mithila was an ancient kingdom located in the eastern part of the Indian subcontinent. It was known as the cultural and educational center of ancient India, and the region is still known as Mithilanchal today. The kingdom was ruled by the Videha and later the Shakya dynasties, and was a major center of the Mauryan Empire.

Mithil was also the birthplace of the revered Hindu goddess, Maitreya, who is considered an embodiment of the future Buddha. The name 'Mithila' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Mithila', which means 'friendly' or 'affable', and reflects the peaceful and harmonious nature of the region.
